tools.name: open_index
tools.description: Open a Lucene index, read-only, in place of the open one, and describe it as index_info does. If it can't be opened, the index that was open stays open.

path.description: The index directory, or a directory with indexes below it, which open as one. A leading ~ is the user's home; a relative path is against leia's working directory

directory.description: The Lucene Directory to read it through: FS lets Lucene choose, MMAP is MMapDirectory, NIO is NIOFSDirectory. Defaults to leia's --directory

path.description: The absolute path that was opened

luceneRuntime.description: The version of the Lucene that reads the index, such as 10.5.2

server.description: The Elasticsearch or OpenSearch installation whose Lucene reads the index, if one does

maxDoc.description: Documents including deleted ones; document ids go from 0 to maxDoc - 1

skipped.description: Index directories below the path that were left out, and why

indexCount.description: How many index directories were opened

segmentsFile.description: The segments_N file of the commit that was opened, the latest one: what the other tools read. Absent without a reader

luceneVersion.description: The Lucene version that wrote that commit; absent if its commit can't be read

userData.description: The user data of that commit, sorted by key, such as Elasticsearch's history_uuid, max_seq_no and local_checkpoint; absent if there is none

indexes.description: The opened index directories, at most 100, in order. Their paths are the ones check_index takes in only

features.description: What the runtime that reads the index can do; other tools fail with NOT_SUPPORTED

fieldCount.description: How many fields the index has

indexOptions.description: What the postings hold; NONE if the field isn't indexed

docValuesType.description: The kind of doc values; absent without

pointDimensionCount.description: Dimensions of the point values; absent without points

pointBytes.description: Bytes per dimension of the point values: 4 for an int or float, 8 for a long or double; absent without points

vectorDimension.description: Dimensions of the KNN vectors; absent without vectors

vectorEncoding.description: How the KNN vectors are encoded, FLOAT32 or BYTE; absent without vectors

vectorSimilarity.description: How the KNN vectors are compared; COSINE refuses a vector of zeros; absent without vectors

hasTermVectors.description: Present, and true, only if the field has term vectors

docCount.description: Documents with at least one term in the field, deleted ones included; absent without postings

fields.description: The fields, at most 1000, by field number. The index doesn't record which fields are stored: get_document shows a document's stored values

tools.name: index_info
tools.description: Describe the open index: its path, the Lucene that reads it, its document counts, its index directories with their commit's user data, and its fields with how each is indexed. Fails with NO_INDEX_OPEN if no index is open; open_index opens one.

path.description: The absolute path that was opened

luceneRuntime.description: The version of the Lucene that reads the index, such as 10.5.2

server.description: The Elasticsearch or OpenSearch installation whose Lucene reads the index, if one does

maxDoc.description: Documents including deleted ones; document ids go from 0 to maxDoc - 1

skipped.description: Index directories below the path that were left out, and why

indexCount.description: How many index directories were opened

segmentsFile.description: The segments_N file of the commit that was opened, the latest one: what the other tools read. Absent without a reader

luceneVersion.description: The Lucene version that wrote that commit; absent if its commit can't be read

userData.description: The user data of that commit, sorted by key, such as Elasticsearch's history_uuid, max_seq_no and local_checkpoint; absent if there is none

indexes.description: The opened index directories, at most 100, in order. Their paths are the ones check_index takes in only

features.description: What the runtime that reads the index can do; other tools fail with NOT_SUPPORTED

fieldCount.description: How many fields the index has

indexOptions.description: What the postings hold; NONE if the field isn't indexed

docValuesType.description: The kind of doc values; absent without

pointDimensionCount.description: Dimensions of the point values; absent without points

pointBytes.description: Bytes per dimension of the point values: 4 for an int or float, 8 for a long or double; absent without points

vectorDimension.description: Dimensions of the KNN vectors; absent without vectors

vectorEncoding.description: How the KNN vectors are encoded, FLOAT32 or BYTE; absent without vectors

vectorSimilarity.description: How the KNN vectors are compared; COSINE refuses a vector of zeros; absent without vectors

hasTermVectors.description: Present, and true, only if the field has term vectors

docCount.description: Documents with at least one term in the field, deleted ones included; absent without postings

fields.description: The fields, at most 1000, by field number. The index doesn't record which fields are stored: get_document shows a document's stored values

tools.name: check_index
tools.description: Check the open index for corruption with Lucene's CheckIndex, read-only. Level 1 verifies checksums; 2 and 3 go deeper and take longer. Narrow a large index with only: paths and segments.

level.description: How thoroughly, from 1 to 3: 1 verifies the checksums of every file (the default), 2 also checks every part of each segment, 3 also runs the slow checks

path.description: The index directory, as index_info lists it in indexes or skipped

segments.description: The segments of its commit to check, such as _0, not empty; all of them by default

only.description: The indexes, and in them the segments, to check; all of them by default. Narrow a large index down: a check of every segment can take long

clean.description: Whether no problem was found in any index

skipped.description: Present, and true, only for an index that was left out when the path was opened

error.description: Why the index couldn't be checked at all, such as no segments_N; then the rest says nothing

segmentsFile.description: The segments_N file of the latest commit, which is the one checked

missingSegments.description: Present, and true, only if the latest commit or an older one couldn't be read

toolOutOfDate.description: Present, and true, only if a newer Lucene than leia's wrote the index

invalidCounter.description: Present, and true, only if the commit's counter for segment names is not above every segment's name

segmentCount.description: The segments of the latest commit

badSegments.description: The segments that failed a test; absent if 0

lostDocs.description: The documents in the bad segments; absent if 0

codec.description: The segment's codec, if its .si file could be read

error.description: The test it failed and why, with the causes

failedSegments.description: The segments that failed, with why; the ones that passed aren't listed. Absent if none

onlySegments.description: The segments that were asked for with only; absent if the whole index was

segmentsNotFound.description: The segments asked for that aren't in the latest commit; then clean is false. Absent if none

indexes.description: Each index checked: the opened ones in order, then the skipped ones

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the open index, best score first unless sort says otherwise, a page at a time: each hit with its document id, score and a few brief stored values, to find documents; get_document and get_field_value read them. Give a query in Lucene's syntax with a defaultField, a term for an exact keyword, docValues for a field that has only those, or knn for the nearest documents to a vector or a document's. For the next page, call it again with the result's nextOffset.

query.description: A query in Lucene's syntax, such as title:lamp AND body:qu*. Ranges on point fields work, such as price:[10 TO 20]; dates on point fields are epoch milliseconds, and dates indexed as text are written as they are indexed, such as published:[20260131 TO 20260228]. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

value.description: The term as text, or in hex with binary

binary.description: Whether value is the term's bytes in hex; false by default

term.description: A query for exactly one term, neither analyzed nor split: for keyword fields such as ids. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

number.description: How a numeric field's values are encoded; LONG by default. DOUBLE and FLOAT are raw bits, SORTABLE_DOUBLE and SORTABLE_FLOAT as Lucene's DoubleField and FloatField write them; get_document's asStored says which. Absent for a field of bytes

values.description: Match documents with a value equal to one of these: decimal text for a number. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

lower.description: The lower bound; absent for none

upper.description: The upper bound; absent for none

includeLower.description: Whether the lower bound matches; true by default

includeUpper.description: Whether the upper bound matches; true by default

range.description: Match documents with a value in this range. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

prefix.description: Match documents with a value that starts with this, for a field of bytes. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

binary.description: Whether values, the bounds and prefix are bytes in hex; false by default

docValues.description: A query on the doc values of a field, for fields that have only those. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

field.description: A field with KNN vectors; index_info shows vectorDimension, vectorEncoding and vectorSimilarity

vector.description: The target vector. For a BYTE field the values are whole numbers from -128 to 127. Give exactly one of vector and docId

docId.description: A document whose vector in field is the target, such as a hit's docId; it may be deleted. Give exactly one of vector and docId

k.description: How many nearest documents to find, from 1 to 10000; in search offset + limit by default, so a page is the k nearest and a higher k lets later pages follow; in explain the most, so pass the search's k to explain a hit as ranked. Not with exact

exact.description: Whether to score every document with a vector instead of searching the graph, and so find all of them as hits; false by default

filter.description: Search only documents that match this query in Lucene's syntax, parsed with defaultField, analyzer, fieldAnalyzers and defaultOperator; ranges on point fields don't work

knn.description: The nearest documents to a vector or to a document's vector, by KNN vectors; the score is the similarity. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

pointTypes.description: The type of point fields in query, when the guess is wrong: a point field of 4 bytes is taken as INT and one of 8 bytes as LONG, so FLOAT and DOUBLE fields need it (index_info shows pointBytes). Goes with query

defaultField.description: The field of the query's terms that name none; needed with query

analyzer.description: The analyzer of query, by simple or class name, such as EnglishAnalyzer or KeywordAnalyzer; StandardAnalyzer by default. Fields indexed with another need theirs

fieldAnalyzers.description: Fields with an analyzer of their own, such as KeywordAnalyzer for ids

defaultOperator.description: How clauses of the query without an operator combine; OR by default

field.description: A field with doc values (not BINARY), or _score or _doc

type.description: How a field's doc values are read: STRING for SORTED and SORTED_SET, else LONG by default. DoubleDocValuesField and FloatDocValuesField need DOUBLE or FLOAT; get_document's asStored says which. Not for _score and _doc

reverse.description: Largest first, or for _score lowest first; false by default

selector.description: Which value of a multi-valued field sorts: MIN by default; SORTED_NUMERIC takes MIN or MAX. Not for _score and _doc

missing.description: Where documents without a value go: LAST by default. Not for _score and _doc

sort.description: The order of the hits, one key after the other; best score first by default. Needs a runtime with SCORING

fields.description: The stored fields to show per hit; by default as many as fit about 250 characters per hit, the rest named in moreFields; [] for none

maxValueLength.description: The longest value shown, in characters, from 1 to 256; 100 by default. get_field_value has a value whole

offset.description: How many hits to skip, for the next page: the nextOffset of the last page; 0 by default

limit.description: The most hits of the page, from 1 to 100; 10 by default

exactTotalHits.description: Whether to count every hit; otherwise counting stops after 1000; false by default

query.description: The query as Lucene writes it

totalHitsRelation.description: Whether totalHits is exact (EQUAL_TO) or a lower bound

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; absent on the last page

value.description: The value; absent for a document without one

binary.description: Present, and true, only if value is in hex

sortValues.description: The values the hit sorted by, one per sort key; absent without sort

value.description: The value; numbers in decimal; binary values as text if they are UTF-8, else in hex

binary.description: Present, and true, only if value is in hex

cut.description: Present, and true, only if value is cut; get_field_value has it whole

fields.description: The hit's stored values, in the order of each field's first value

moreFields.description: Stored fields left out to keep the page short; name them in fields, or read them with get_document. Absent if none was

hits.description: The hits of the page, best score first unless sort says otherwise

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Explain how a document scores for a query, or why it doesn't match: the arguments of search plus a hit's docId. Lucene's explanation, one line per part, indented.

query.description: A query in Lucene's syntax, such as title:lamp AND body:qu*. Ranges on point fields work, such as price:[10 TO 20]; dates on point fields are epoch milliseconds, and dates indexed as text are written as they are indexed, such as published:[20260131 TO 20260228]. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

value.description: The term as text, or in hex with binary

binary.description: Whether value is the term's bytes in hex; false by default

term.description: A query for exactly one term, neither analyzed nor split: for keyword fields such as ids. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

number.description: How a numeric field's values are encoded; LONG by default. DOUBLE and FLOAT are raw bits, SORTABLE_DOUBLE and SORTABLE_FLOAT as Lucene's DoubleField and FloatField write them; get_document's asStored says which. Absent for a field of bytes

values.description: Match documents with a value equal to one of these: decimal text for a number. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

lower.description: The lower bound; absent for none

upper.description: The upper bound; absent for none

includeLower.description: Whether the lower bound matches; true by default

includeUpper.description: Whether the upper bound matches; true by default

range.description: Match documents with a value in this range. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

prefix.description: Match documents with a value that starts with this, for a field of bytes. Give exactly one of values, range and prefix

binary.description: Whether values, the bounds and prefix are bytes in hex; false by default

docValues.description: A query on the doc values of a field, for fields that have only those. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

field.description: A field with KNN vectors; index_info shows vectorDimension, vectorEncoding and vectorSimilarity

vector.description: The target vector. For a BYTE field the values are whole numbers from -128 to 127. Give exactly one of vector and docId

docId.description: A document whose vector in field is the target, such as a hit's docId; it may be deleted. Give exactly one of vector and docId

k.description: How many nearest documents to find, from 1 to 10000; in search offset + limit by default, so a page is the k nearest and a higher k lets later pages follow; in explain the most, so pass the search's k to explain a hit as ranked. Not with exact

exact.description: Whether to score every document with a vector instead of searching the graph, and so find all of them as hits; false by default

filter.description: Search only documents that match this query in Lucene's syntax, parsed with defaultField, analyzer, fieldAnalyzers and defaultOperator; ranges on point fields don't work

knn.description: The nearest documents to a vector or to a document's vector, by KNN vectors; the score is the similarity. Give exactly one of query, term, docValues and knn

pointTypes.description: The type of point fields in query, when the guess is wrong: a point field of 4 bytes is taken as INT and one of 8 bytes as LONG, so FLOAT and DOUBLE fields need it (index_info shows pointBytes). Goes with query

defaultField.description: The field of the query's terms that name none; needed with query

analyzer.description: The analyzer of query, by simple or class name, such as EnglishAnalyzer or KeywordAnalyzer; StandardAnalyzer by default. Fields indexed with another need theirs

fieldAnalyzers.description: Fields with an analyzer of their own, such as KeywordAnalyzer for ids

defaultOperator.description: How clauses of the query without an operator combine; OR by default

docId.description: The document to explain: the docId of a hit of search

maxLines.description: The most lines of the explanation, from 1 to 10000; 200 by default. It is cut at a whole line

matches.description: Whether the document matches the query

score.description: The document's score; absent if it doesn't match

explanation.description: Lucene's explanation: one line per part, as value = description, with the parts of a line indented below it. For a document that doesn't match, why not

cut.description: Present, and true, only if lines were left out; call again with a higher maxLines

tools.name: scan_stored
tools.description: Find stored values by a Java regex, also in fields that aren't indexed, such as _source. Scans documents in id order and stops once the page is full; for the next page, call again with nextOffset. Slow on large indexes: narrow it with fields.

pattern.description: A Java regular expression, found anywhere in a value; flags go inline, such as (?s)

caseInsensitive.description: Whether case doesn't matter; false by default

fields.description: The stored fields to scan; all of them by default, which takes long on a large index

includeDeleted.description: Whether to scan deleted documents too; false by default

offset.description: The hits to skip: the nextOffset of the last page; 0 by default. Every page scans from the first document again

limit.description: The most hits of the page, from 1 to 100; 20 by default

deleted.description: Present, and true, only for a deleted document

valueIndex.description: Which of the document's stored values in the field, as get_field_value takes it; absent if 0

length.description: The length of the whole value in bytes

matchCount.description: How many matches the value has; absent if 1

snippet.description: The value around the first match: about 40 characters before it, 160 after

match.description: The text of the first match, cut at the end of the snippet if it runs past it

hits.description: The values with a match, in document order

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page, which has hits; absent on the last page

scannedDocs.description: The document ids gone through, deleted ones included; with stopped, at least that many

stopped.description: Present, and true, only if the scan stopped once the page was full: the counts cover scannedDocs only

matchedValues.description: The values with a match among the scanned documents

matchedDocs.description: The documents with a match; absent unless the scan went through the whole index

timedOutValues.description: The values that were skipped because matching them took more than a second: simplify the pattern. Absent unless the scan went through the whole index, and if there were none

tools.name: analyze
tools.description: What an analyzer makes of a text: its tokens with positions, offsets and types, to see why a query matches or not and which analyzer a field needs. Needs no open index.

text.description: The text to analyze, at most 10000 characters

analyzer.description: By simple or class name, as in search; StandardAnalyzer by default

maxTokens.description: The most tokens shown, from 1 to 10000; 200 by default

startOffset.description: Where the token starts in the text

endOffset.description: Where the token ends in the text

positionLength.description: How many positions the token spans; absent if 1

tokenCount.description: The tokens the text makes, counted up to 10000

cut.description: Present, and true, only if tokens are left out

tools.name: terms
tools.description: List the terms of a field, as the index holds them after analysis: the values to search for, and why a term query misses. A page in term order, optionally from a prefix, or with top the terms in the most documents. Counts include deleted documents. For the next page, call it again with the result's next as from and the same prefix.

prefix.description: Only terms that start with this text; a binary term never does

value.description: The term as text, or in hex with binary

binary.description: Whether value is the term's bytes in hex; false by default

from.description: Where the page starts: the next of the last page, which continues it with the same prefix

limit.description: The most terms of the page, from 1 to 1000; 50 by default

top.description: Instead of a page, the N terms in the most documents, from 1 to 1000, most first: it scans every term of the field, which takes long on a large one. Excludes prefix, from and limit

binary.description: Present, and true, only if term is the term's bytes in hex

docFreq.description: The documents with the term, deleted ones included

totalTermFreq.description: The occurrences of the term in all documents; absent if equal to docFreq

terms.description: The terms, in term order, or with top, most documents first

value.description: The term as text, or in hex with binary

binary.description: Whether value is the term's bytes in hex; false by default

next.description: The from of the next page; absent after the last term, and with top

uniqueTerms.description: How many distinct terms the field has; with top only

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Show a document of the open index by its id: per field its stored values, doc values, norm, KNN vector and whether it has a term vector. Long values are cut, with their full length; get_field_value reads one whole. Fields that are only indexed show no value: reconstruct_fields rebuilds them.

docId.description: The document id, from 0 to maxDoc - 1; a deleted document can be read too

fields.description: The fields to show, in the index's order; by default every field the document has something in

maxValueLength.description: The longest value shown whole, in characters, up to 65536; 2048 by default. get_field_value has a longer one whole

withVectors.description: Whether to show the components of KNN vectors; otherwise only their dimension; false by default

deleted.description: Whether the document is deleted; its data is there until a merge

norm.description: The document's norm; absent without norms

value.description: The value; numbers in decimal; binary values as text if they are UTF-8, else in hex

binary.description: Present, and true, only if value is in hex

fullLength.description: Present if value is cut: the length of the whole value in characters; get_field_value has the rest

stored.description: The stored values, in the order they were added; absent if none are stored

count.description: How many values the document has

numbers.description: The raw numbers of a NUMERIC or SORTED_NUMERIC field, in decimal as strings (a JSON number loses digits beyond 2^53), at most 100; absent for the other types, and with asStored

asStored.description: Present if the numbers are the field's stored values in this encoding (a double's bits, say); numbers is then left out, and the stored values are the numbers

value.description: The bytes as text if they are UTF-8, else in hex

binary.description: Present, and true, only if value is in hex

fullLength.description: Present if value is cut: the length of the whole value in characters

values.description: The values of a BINARY, SORTED or SORTED_SET field, at most 100; absent for the other types

docValues.description: The document's doc values; absent if it has none in the field

hasTermVector.description: Present, and true, only if the document has a term vector in the field

floats.description: The components of a FLOAT32 vector, with withVectors

bytes.description: The components of a BYTE vector, signed, with withVectors

vector.description: The document's KNN vector; absent if it has none in the field

fields.description: The fields, in the index's order

tools.name: get_field_value
tools.description: Read one stored value of a document whole, in slices of characters: for a value that get_document or search cut. Call it again with nextOffset until it is absent.

index.description: Which of the document's stored values in the field, from 0, as get_document lists them; 0 by default

offset.description: Where the slice starts, in characters: the nextOffset of the last slice; 0 by default

length.description: The most characters of the slice, up to 65536; 16384 by default

binary.description: Whether value is in hex: a binary value that isn't UTF-8

totalLength.description: The length of the whole value in characters

nextOffset.description: Where the next slice starts; absent at the end of the value

tools.name: reconstruct_fields
tools.description: Rebuild the terms and points a document was indexed with, field by field, from its term vectors or the postings: what an indexed field holds even if it isn't stored. With positions, text gives the terms in order, and stands for the terms unless withTerms is set. It goes through every term of a field without a term vector, which can take a while in a large index.

docId.description: The document id, from 0 to maxDoc - 1; a deleted document is rebuilt too

fields.description: The fields with postings or points to rebuild, in this order; by default every such field

maxTerms.description: The most terms per field in terms, up to 10000; 500 by default

withTerms.description: Whether to list the terms with their freqs and positions also where text has them; false by default

indexOptions.description: What the postings of the field hold in the document's segment

source.description: Where the terms come from: the document's TERM_VECTOR, or the POSTINGS of every term

text.description: The terms in position order, as the analyzer left the text: terms at one position joined with |, a gap of positions as …; absent without positions

textCut.description: Present, and true, only if text is cut at 65536 characters

term.description: The term as text, or in hex with binary

binary.description: Present, and true, only if term is in hex

freq.description: How often the term occurs in the field of the document

positions.description: Its positions, at most 1000; absent without positions

terms.description: The terms in term order, at most maxTerms; absent where text has them, unless withTerms

termCount.description: How many terms the document has in the field

cut.description: Present, and true, only if terms holds fewer than termCount

dimensions.description: The bytes of each dimension in lowercase hex, as Lucene packs them: sortable and big-endian, for IntPoint and the like

points.description: The document's points, at most 100, in unsigned byte order; absent without

pointCount.description: How many points the document has in the field; absent without

fields.description: The fields in the order they were asked for
